newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Philippine farmers' group denied a police intelligence report linking the organisation to an alleged plot to sabotage the APEC summit next month at the Subic freeport (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The Commission on Human Rights backed the government's demolition of squatter shanties in Metro Manila. Commission chairperson Aurora Recina said the squatters could not accuse the government of violating their rights since it was the government's duty to protect them. She said the squatters were being cleared from river banks and other places which were considered dangerous. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- German chancellor Helmut Kohl will arrive today for a three day state visit and a series of talks with President Fidel Ramos to strengthen Philippine-German relations, specially in trade and investments (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Transport groups in various parts of the country pushed through with a strike on Monday to call for a fare rise because of oil price increases (TODAY)
